PureScore.purpose: Aggregates pillar risks into a single 0-100 headline score via confidence-weighted power-mean (δ=2), then enforces the critical cascade cap (≤40 when any pillar is critical); each computation is persisted as an immutable snapshot with the full explanation object.

stories.want: my PureScore to be immediately capped at or below 40 whenever a life-threatening biomarker is critical
stories.soThat: I and my clinician see unambiguous urgency and cannot be falsely reassured by healthy pillars averaging away the danger
acceptance: Given a patient with K⁺=6.3 and all other pillars green, When the scoring engine runs, Then PureScore ≤ 40 and overall_status = CRITICAL

Given a patient where the critical marker is flagged as a lab artifact (confidence≈0 per D14), When the engine runs, Then the cascade does NOT fire and PureScore is computed normally with a Reconfirm-pending flag
Given a patient whose K⁺ drops below the red threshold on re-test, When the engine runs without confirming-measurement hysteresis cleared, Then PureScore remains capped until hysteresis resolves
edge: Two simultaneous critical markers in different pillars: cascade must still cap at 40 and surface both binding constraints in the explanation
Model-version change mid-flight: snapshot must record the model_version_id at the time of computation so audits are reproducible

stories.want: my PureScore to tick up visibly the day after I get a good night's sleep or complete 9,000 steps
stories.soThat: daily positive actions produce real, immediate feedback reinforcing the behaviour loop
acceptance: Given a patient's personal baseline for sleep duration is μ=6.5h and they log 8h, When the scoring engine runs Stage 2b, Then r_i^pers = κ_resp·tanh(z/2) with z<0 and PureScore rises by a measurable non-zero delta
Given κ_resp=0.10 and band_clamp active, When the personal-baseline term is computed, Then the resulting r_i never falls below the Stage 2 clinical/cohort floor (band_clamp cannot relax a red)
Given the pillar is already red/critical, When Stage 2b runs, Then the 𝟙[non-critical] flag suppresses the personal-baseline additive term entirely
edge: Cold-start patient with fewer than the minimum measurement count: empirical-Bayes shrinks to cohort prior; z-score weight is low so feedback signal is small but still non-zero

stories.want: to retrieve the binding constraint (which pillar and marker capped the score) with every score fetch
stories.soThat: I can immediately focus on the correct clinical concern without reading the full explanation object
acceptance: Given a patient with a critical REN pillar, When GET /v1/patients/{id}/score is called, Then the response includes cappedBy: {pillar:'REN', marker:'K+', escalation:'emergency'}
Given all pillars are on-track, When GET /v1/patients/{id}/score is called, Then cappedBy is null and overall_status = ON_TRACK
Given overall_status = AT_RISK (R_total ≥ 0.30 but no critical), When score is fetched, Then cappedBy is null and PureScore = PureScore° without cascade
edge: Score requested before any measurements exist: return 404 or a coverage=0 sentinel score clearly marked insufficient-data, never a fabricated value

stories.want: every PureScore snapshot to be deterministic and immutable given its inputs and model version
stories.soThat: audit trails and regulatory reviews can reproduce any historical score exactly
acceptance: Given identical input measurements and the same model_version_id, When the scoring engine runs twice, Then both snapshots have identical value, status, and explanation JSON
Given a constant change triggers a model-version bump per D20, When the new version is applied, Then old snapshots retain the old model_version_id and are not retroactively altered
Given admin-constants is called with a valid proposal, When the gate passes, Then a new model_version record is created and all subsequent score snapshots reference it
edge: Concurrent ingest events for the same patient within the same second: idempotency-key dedup must prevent double-computation; last-write-wins with the newer measurement timestamp

table.name: pure_score_snapshot

columns.name: is_cold_start
columns.note: true when personal baseline still shrunk to cohort prior

table.notes: Time-series; range-partitioned by computed_at (monthly). Append-only — no UPDATE or DELETE. Latest snapshot per patient is the live score; historical rows are the audit trail. Partition pruning on patient_id + computed_at for GET /score (latest row) and for validation-harness batch reads.

invariants: IF any pillar status = CRITICAL THEN value ≤ PURE_CRIT_CAP (40) — hard cap, never relaxable by personalisation
value = 100·(1 − R_total) before cascade; cascade only lowers, never raises the value
overall_status = CRITICAL IFF ∃ pillar with status = CRITICAL; AT_RISK IFF R_total ≥ 0.30 AND no critical; ON_TRACK otherwise
model_version_id MUST be set on every snapshot; orphaned snapshots (no FK) are invalid
Append-only: no row may be updated or deleted after insert; corrections are new snapshots referencing a correction note
Determinism: given same (patient_id, set_of_measurement_ids, model_version_id), value is bit-identical across recomputes
band_clamp: Stage 2b personalisation cannot set r_i below the Stage 2 clinical/cohort floor, so no personal-baseline improvement can relax a red or clear a critical
escalation = emergency MUST trigger the emergency pathway (Doc 16); no silent suppression except via confirmed data-quality confidence≈0 flag (D14)

Pillar.purpose: Aggregates marker risks for one organ-system domain into a pillar risk R_k via γ=3 confidence-weighted power mean plus a reservoir load term, determines the pillar's status (green/yellow/red/critical), and exposes per-pillar score S_k, coverage, and top contributors for the explanation and clinician view.

stories.want: the worst marker in a pillar to dominate the pillar score even when my other markers in that pillar are green
stories.soThat: a single dangerous value cannot be averaged away and hidden
acceptance: Given a CV pillar with systolic BP r=0.7 (red) and three other markers all r=0.05 (green), When pillar aggregation runs with γ=3, Then R_CV is substantially closer to 0.7 than to the simple average of all four markers
Given R_k ≥ 0.60, When status is computed, Then status_k = critical regardless of whether a specific critical-marker flag is set
Given a critical-marker (e.g. eGFR) with r_i ≥ 0.5 in REN pillar, When status is computed, Then status_k = critical and R_k is floored to max(R_k, R_crit=0.60)
edge: All markers in a pillar are imputed (confidence low): coverage cov_k < threshold → pillar displayed as low-coverage-green, not confirmed-green; S_k is shown with a data-gap caveat

stories.want: to see pillar coverage alongside the score so I know when a green pillar is green by default vs evidenced
stories.soThat: I do not over-interpret a pillar score based on absent data
acceptance: Given a pillar with 3 of 6 markers observed and the rest literature-imputed, When GET /v1/patients/{id}/pillars is called, Then cov_k = observed_weight / total_weight < 1.0 and a low_coverage flag is set
Given cov_k is below the green-display threshold, When the pillar is returned, Then status may not be displayed as confirmed-green even if R_k < 0.15
Given all markers are observed with full confidence, When coverage is computed, Then cov_k = 1.0 and no caveat is added
edge: Marker added to a pillar mid-model-version: historical pillar snapshots retain the old coverage denominator; the new marker only affects snapshots after the model-version bump

stories.want: the reservoir load term to raise a pillar's risk even when its spot markers look acceptable
stories.soThat: chronic burden (e.g. accumulated sleep debt on SLP/CV) is reflected in the pillar risk continuously
acceptance: Given B̃_SLP = 0.8 (high chronic sleep debt) and ρ_SLP = 0.2, When pillar risk is computed, Then R_SLP = clamp(R_SLP^mark + 0.2·0.8) = clamp(R_SLP^mark + 0.16) which is ≥ R_SLP^mark
Given ρ_k = 0.20 and B̃_k = 1.0, When the reservoir term is added, Then the maximum reservoir contribution is 0.20 and R_k is clamped to [0,1]
Given reservoir load is zero (B̃_k=0), When pillar risk is computed, Then R_k = R_k^mark with no reservoir contribution
edge: A pillar receives contributions from multiple reservoirs (e.g. ALLO and SLP both feed MCS): B̃_k is the aggregate normalized load; individual reservoir contributions must be decomposed in the explanation for nudge attribution

table.name: pillar_snapshot

columns.name: pillar_code
columns.note: CV | MET | FIT | MCS | SLP | REN | HEP | IMM | END | HEM | MSK | GI | PUL

table.notes: Appended with each PureScore recompute; one row per pillar per snapshot. Range-partitioned by computed_at. Never updated after insert.

invariants: status = critical IFF (∃ i∈k with r_i ≥ 0.5 AND i ∈ CriticalMarkers_k) OR R_k ≥ 0.60 — both conditions independently sufficient
IF status = critical THEN r_k ≥ R_crit (0.60) — risk is floored, never below the critical floor
s_k = 100·(1 − r_k); s_k ≤ 40 when status = critical
reservoir_contribution ≤ ρ_k · 1.0 (i.e. ≤ 0.20 at default ρ) — reservoir term is bounded
r_k = clamp([0,1], r_k_mark + reservoir_contribution) — clamp ensures r_k stays in unit interval
cov_k = Σ(observed ŵ_i) / Σ(all ŵ_i); low cov_k triggers low-coverage display suppression of confirmed-green
pillar_code must exist in the versioned pillar catalogue for the given model_version_id; orphaned codes are rejected on insert

CriticalCascade.purpose: Implements the safety override that floors any critical pillar's risk to R_crit=0.60, caps PureScore at PURE_CRIT_CAP=40 when any pillar is critical, sets overall_status=CRITICAL, and fires the emergency or urgent escalation pathway for acute-danger markers — ensuring a single life-threatening biomarker is never averaged away.

stories.want: a confirmed acute-danger critical marker to unconditionally trigger the emergency escalation pathway
stories.soThat: no clinical emergency can be silenced by healthy pillars or a high background PureScore
acceptance: Given K⁺=6.3 with escalation=emergency and confidence=1.0, When CriticalCascade runs, Then overall_status=CRITICAL, PureScore≤40, and the emergency pathway (Doc 16) is triggered within the same compute cycle
Given SpO2=88% from a consumer-tier wearable (confidence≈0 per D14/D22), When CriticalCascade runs, Then the cascade does NOT fire; an Early-warning Watch is raised instead
Given SpO2=88% corroborated by a second clinical-grade device (confidence=1.0), When CriticalCascade runs, Then the cascade fires and escalation=emergency is routed to the clinician
edge: Emergency escalation must fire even if the patient has previously opted out of notifications: the safety pathway bypasses nudge-preference settings (Doc 16 compliance)

stories.want: the cascade to lift when I re-test and the critical marker is confirmed normal, but not instantaneously flip back on noise
stories.soThat: my score recovers honestly when the danger resolves without oscillating on measurement noise
acceptance: Given a patient exiting a critical state (K⁺ returned to 5.0), When the confirming measurement arrives, Then the cascade flag is removed only after hysteresis clearance (either confirming-measurement or sustained reservoir drain per Doc 03 §6)
Given only one in-range re-test with no sustained improvement, When CriticalCascade evaluates, Then status remains critical-pending-confirmation and PureScore stays capped
Given two consecutive in-range measurements with no adverse reservoir state, When CriticalCascade evaluates, Then the floor is lifted and PureScore rebounds to PureScore°
edge: Anti-flap: a borderline marker oscillating around the critical threshold (r=0.49/0.51) must require hysteresis to settle before status toggles — bare threshold crossing must not cause same-day flip/unflip

stories.want: to distinguish reserve-deficit critical markers from acute-danger critical markers in the cascade output
stories.soThat: the engine routes reserve-deficit reds to improvement plans rather than the emergency pathway
acceptance: Given VO2max in the very-low range (reserve-deficit critical, escalation=routine), When CriticalCascade runs, Then pillar is floored to R_crit, PureScore≤40, but escalation=routine and the improvement plan path (Doc 09) is triggered — NOT emergency
Given PHQ-9 item 9 score ≥ 3 (suicidality, escalation=emergency), When CriticalCascade runs, Then escalation=emergency and the crisis pathway is triggered immediately
Given escalation field missing from the marker catalogue, When CriticalCascade runs, Then computation halts and returns an error — untagged critical markers are forbidden
edge: Multiple simultaneous critical markers with mixed escalation levels: the highest escalation level (emergency > urgent > routine) governs the pathway fired; all critical markers are listed in the explanation

table.name: critical_cascade_event

columns.name: pure_score_snapshot_id
columns.note: score snapshot that fired this event

columns.name: hysteresis_cleared
columns.note: false until confirmed normal or reservoir drained

columns.name: artifact_suppressed
columns.note: true if cascade was blocked by confidence≈0 flag (D14)

table.notes: Append-only audit log of every cascade firing and resolution. One row per cascade event (not per snapshot). resolved_at is set when hysteresis clears. artifact_suppressed=true rows are Watch events, not real cascades — kept for audit completeness.

invariants: IF escalation_level = emergency AND artifact_suppressed = false THEN pathway_triggered = emergency — no silent suppression of confirmed emergencies
pure_score_after_cap ≤ 40 — the cap is absolute; no pillar weight configuration may override it
resolved_at IS NULL implies the cascade is still active and the current score snapshot must still be capped
artifact_suppressed = true requires a data-quality confidence≈0 flag from the ingestion layer — cascade cannot be suppressed by any business logic
hysteresis_cleared = true requires either a confirmed in-range measurement OR sustained reservoir drainage, never just a single re-test at the margin
triggering_marker_ids must reference markers in the CriticalMarkers catalogue for the active model_version; uncatalogued markers may not fire a cascade
escalation_level = max(escalation of all triggering markers) — highest severity governs the pathway

PersonalBaseline.purpose: Maintains each patient's per-marker empirical-Bayes personal baseline (μ_i^p, σ_i^p) that powers Stage 2b personalised responsiveness and the companion Trajectory, Early-warning, and Modifiability dimensions; cold-starts shrunk to the cohort prior and converges to personal statistics as measurements accumulate.

stories.want: my baseline for each marker to start from population norms and smoothly personalise as my readings accumulate
stories.soThat: I get honest feedback from day one without needing months of data
acceptance: Given a new patient with zero prior readings for HRV, When the personal baseline is requested, Then μ_i^p = cohort_mean and σ_i^p = cohort_sd with shrinkage_weight = 0.0 (fully cold-start)
Given a patient with 30 daily HRV readings, When the baseline is updated, Then shrinkage_weight > 0.5 and μ_i^p has moved meaningfully toward the patient's empirical mean
Given a heavy-tailed marker (hsCRP, flagged skew=true per D13), When the baseline is updated, Then μ_i^p and σ_i^p are computed on log(value) and the z-score is on the log scale
edge: Patient with a single outlier reading early in their history: empirical-Bayes shrinkage must dampen the outlier's influence; a single extreme value should not permanently skew the baseline

stories.want: the personal z-score to drive the Stage 2b term and correctly orient adverse direction per marker
stories.soThat: improvement-vs-your-baseline always lowers r_i and degradation always raises it, with correct polarity per marker
acceptance: Given a patient whose resting HR (adverse direction = high) drops below their personal mean, When Stage 2b computes z_i = sign_adverse·(x_i − μ_i^p)/σ_i^p, Then z_i < 0 and r_i^pers = κ_resp·tanh(z_i/2) < 0, reducing r_i
Given a patient whose HDL (adverse direction = low) rises above their personal mean, When Stage 2b runs, Then z_i < 0 and r_i decreases
Given z_i = 2.0 and κ_resp = 0.10, When r_i^pers is computed, Then r_i^pers = 0.10·tanh(1.0) ≈ 0.076 and the result is bounded to [−0.10, +0.10]
edge: σ_i^p → 0 (patient has near-constant readings): denominator clamp must prevent z-score explosion; minimum σ is floored to a fraction of cohort σ

stories.want: to see the trajectory and early-warning signals derived from the personal baseline history
stories.soThat: I can detect adverse trends before any clinical band is crossed
acceptance: Given a patient whose sleep duration z-scores have been positive (worse-than-baseline) for 7 consecutive days, When the companion vector is computed, Then Trajectory for SLP is flagged as declining and an Early-warning Watch is raised
Given z-scores return to negative after the adverse streak, When the companion is recomputed, Then the Watch flag is downgraded (with hysteresis) and Trajectory shows recovering

Given the diagonal-covariance aggregate D = sqrt(Σzᵢ²) exceeds the Advisory threshold across multiple markers simultaneously, When early-warning runs, Then an Advisory (not just Watch) is surfaced per D10
edge: Patient on a new medication that systematically shifts a biomarker (e.g. statin lowers LDL): the personal baseline will appear to improve rapidly; the engine must not interpret the drug-effect step-change as an adverse-to-normal rebound — medication context (D3) should flag the reading as MANAGED with down-weight on the baseline z

stories.want: each baseline update to be stored as a versioned snapshot so the history of baseline parameters is auditable
stories.soThat: we can replay any historical z-score computation from stored parameters
acceptance: Given a new measurement is ingested, When the baseline updater runs, Then a new personal_baseline_snapshot row is inserted with updated_at = now() and the prior row is not modified

Given a request to audit a past PureScore, When the audit lookup resolves personal_baseline_snapshot rows by patient_id + marker_id + updated_at ≤ score.computed_at, Then the parameters at the time of the score are recovered exactly
Given the baseline for a skew-tagged marker, When the row is read, Then log_scale = true and mu and sigma are stored in log-space
edge: Bulk historical data upload (e.g. 2 years of wearable data imported on onboarding): baseline must be computed in chronological order over the import batch; out-of-order processing must be detected and rejected or re-sorted

table.name: personal_baseline_snapshot

columns.name: mu_personal
columns.note: empirical-Bayes blended mean; log-space if log_scale=true

columns.name: sigma_personal
columns.note: blended std dev; floored to avoid division-by-zero

columns.name: mu_cohort
columns.note: cohort prior mean at time of update

columns.name: n_obs
columns.note: number of observations used to compute personal stats

table.notes: Time-series; range-partitioned by updated_at (monthly). Append-only — each measurement update appends a new row. Latest row per (patient_id, marker_id) is the live baseline. Historical rows enable exact replay of any past z-score. sigma_personal is clamped to max(computed_sigma, cohort_sigma·MIN_SIGMA_FRACTION) to prevent z-score explosion.

invariants: sigma_personal > 0 — enforced via floor at MAX(computed_sigma, cohort_sigma·MIN_SIGMA_FRACTION); zero-sigma rows are forbidden
shrinkage_weight ∈ [0,1]; shrinkage_weight = 0 when n_obs < minimum cold-start threshold (per-marker config)
log_scale = true IFF the marker catalogue tags the marker as skew; this flag is immutable for a given marker across all rows
sign_adverse ∈ {-1, +1}; must match the marker catalogue for the active model_version — mismatched sign inverts the feedback loop and is a critical correctness error
Append-only: no UPDATE or DELETE after insert; the history is the audit trail for companion Trajectory/Early-warning replay
updated_at must be ≥ the updated_at of all prior rows for the same (patient_id, marker_id); out-of-order inserts are rejected
r_i^pers = κ_resp·tanh(z_i/2) ∈ [−κ_resp, +κ_resp] = [−0.10, +0.10]; the additive term is bounded by design and must be enforced at computation time
